suggestions.issue: This is tagged a BEGINNER term, but the third common mistake uses 'mousing it' with no gloss. A beginner reading 'without mousing it or using a bolt-type (safety) shackle' will hit an unexplained term and lose the point of the mistake (which is exactly the safety takeaway they most need to retain).
suggestions.suggestion: Briefly define the term inline, e.g. '...without mousing it (securing the screw pin with wire or a zip tie so vibration cannot back it out) or using a bolt-type (safety) shackle.'

suggestions.issue: For a beginner term, the acronym 'WLL' is used ('reads the WLL stamped on the bow') before it is spelled out anywhere in the edited fields, adding a small comprehension gap on a safety-critical number.
suggestions.suggestion: Spell it out on first use: 'reads the Working Load Limit (WLL) stamped on the bow.'

suggestions.issue: The related_terms list includes the term itself, 'Digital Wireless System'. A self-referencing entry adds nothing to the learner's knowledge map and reads as an error, undermining trust in the cross-links.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace the self-reference with a genuinely adjacent concept that aids contrast/transfer, e.g. 'Analog Wireless System' (to reinforce the compander comparison the definition draws) or 'In-Ear Monitor (IEM)' (the latency-sensitive use case already named in the fields).
